In mathematics, a '''quaternionic discrete series representation''' is a [[discrete series representation]] of a [[semisimple Lie group]] ''G'' associated with a quaternionic structure on the [[symmetric space]] of ''G''. They were introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Gross|last2=Wallach|year1=1994|year2=1996}}. 

Quaternionic discrete series representations exist when the [[maximal compact subgroup]] of the group ''G'' has a [[normal subgroup]] isomorphic to [[SU(2)]]. Every complex simple [[Lie group]] has a real form with quaternionic discrete series representations. In particular the classical groups SU(2,''n''), SO(4,''n''), and Sp(1,''n'') have quaternionic discrete series representations. 

Quaternionic representations are analogous to [[holomorphic discrete series representation]]s, which exist when the symmetric space of the group has a complex structure. The groups SU(2,''n'') have both holomorphic and quaternionic discrete series representations.
